structured_output.summary: Chunk `connection-compatibility` (attempt 2) is genuinely implemented and the attempt-1 findings are resolved in source, not prose. Both attempt-1 medium findings are closed: `tools/g25_report.py:103-129` now generates a separate "Management 0.86.0 projection addendum" (rendered at docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:30-43), qualifies the data-plane sentence ("in the data-plane corpus", :17) and states that `projection-bindings.json` owns only that corpus, with `test_documented_projection_models_cover_both_generators` (tools/test_g25_report.py:109-135) asserting the documented model set equals the union of both mechanisms and that a duplicate binding raises; and the projection/union bindings are no longer bare IDs — `BASELINE_NAMES`/`verify_model_names` pin the expected generated model name for all eight frozen nodes, `extend_nodes` requires each node to be byte-identical to the frozen `contracts/typescript.json` body, and `check_projection_completeness` independently discovers the affected set from the whole frozen graph and fails on omission or an extra node (regressions at tools/test_red_team_management_models.py:49-69). The five attempt-1 lows are also closed: `runtimeEnumExtensions` is now derived from the applied delta (ledger() :252-253, test asserts REALTIME+FUTURE_MODE including duplicate handling and that a mutated production YAML is rejected by the pin); `test_runtime_adoption_rejects_renamed_wire_test` and `…_changed_union_extension_ledger` give the two strongest gate guards negative coverage; `current_schema_enums_have_named_variants_and_frozen_constants_keep_unknowns` proves the Unknown→named transition on the schema-bound enums while the frozen-parity `TargetConnectionType`/`ResponseMode` keep `Unknown(..)` (documented by generated rustdoc at generated.rs:162441, 174151 and `enumCompatibility` in the overlay ledger); `target_response_declarations` records all five operations with per-field vendor/SDK presence-nullability comparison, required-field equality, retained root `s012107`, both response modes, the bound fixture name and an explicit comparison limit (compatibility-decisions.json:4208-7623), asserted by `test_target_response_comparison_records_every_vendor_field_and_retained_root`; the dead overlay write is gone (single write at generate_models.py:1112) and `replace_once` requires exactly one match; the phase-number prose spacing is fixed with an explicit comment that `adoptionState` tokens are machine identifiers (red_team_management.py:522-526). Independently, the design is strong: all four connection-params objects (`s010789/s010821/s010824/s010829`) share the same `s010462`/`s010504` union nodes, so the two reviewed tails cover REST, streaming, WebSocket and the request variant; projections are model-only (absent from schema_graph.json) with lossless raw fallback; the 23 frozen default bindings and `contracts/native-union-variants.json` are untouched; validation.rs adds exactly the three reviewed Vertex patterns and generation fails unless the native regex set equals `REGEX_SOURCES | MANAGEMENT_REGEX_SOURCES`. Evidence is executed, not asserted: the recorded check set is 30+ commands at exit 0, including four `check-rust.py` matrices (1.89.0 and 1.99.0, red-team and red-team+arbitrary_precision) whose output contains the 19 new management test functions passing alongside the pre-existing suite, plus the offline live boundary (liveVerified 0 across native-operations/native-exports/qualification) and a private-material receipt bound to the exact reviewed source hash. Remaining issues are four low precision/evidence gaps, none blocking.

findings.description: `default` is included in the permitted annotation set and is then silently discarded for every field except the reviewed `client_session` const (line 119). Every other runtime-significant keyword in this compiler fails closed: unknown vocabulary (111), unreviewed patterns (130), non-nullable anyOf (115), unreviewed discriminators (120), unreviewed string formats (126). `default` is the one remaining annotation with runtime meaning in this graph (it is what produces a ZodDefault node and what the 23 frozen default bindings are built from), so a re-pinned source that adds a vendor default to any new management field would silently compile to a non-defaulting node with no review signal, while `defaultPolicy` in the overlay ledger continues to claim 'No added default nodes'. The current pin has no such default (VertexAIConnectionParams/openapi.json:9431-9465 and the four projected fields declare none), and SOURCE_SHA256 pinning means a re-pin is a reviewed act, so nothing is wrong in this source state.
findings.required_fix: Reject `default` in tools/red_team_management_models.py:108 outside the reviewed `client_session` discriminator (keep the explicit check at line 119), and add a regression in tools/test_red_team_management_models.py that patches a `default` onto a VertexAIConnectionParams or projection field and expects an 'Unreviewed' ValueError.

findings.description: check_projection_completeness discovers the affected baseline objects from hardcoded legacy property signatures ('basic_auth_location', or the triple {api_endpoint, request_json, multi_turn_config}) rather than from the vendor components that actually declare the projected wire keys. The vendor declares these four keys on eight components — BasicAuthAuthConfig (openapi.json:2636) and BasicAuthAuthConfigRedact (:2695), plus Rest/Streaming/WebSocketConnectionParamsBase (:5501, :5911, :9505) and their three RedactBase counterparts (:5699, :6121, :9713) — but PROJECTIONS (lines 22-29) sources the field schema only from the four non-redact components, with no assertion that the redact counterparts declare an identical schema. A future divergence in a masked declaration (for example a `format: password` plus a different type on basic_password) would be projected with the unredacted shape and no diagnostic, and a new vendor auth variant carrying basic_username would not be discovered because the legacy-side signature would not change. The eight current declarations are equivalent, so this is precision rather than an active defect.
findings.required_fix: Derive the candidate set from the vendor components that declare the projected fields (both plain and Redact), assert that each redact/non-redact pair declares an identical field schema before compiling it, and add regressions in tools/test_red_team_management_models.py for a divergent redact declaration and for a new vendor component that declares one of the four keys.

findings.description: The 12 projection occurrences, two union tails and three enum values have no derived or independently generated corpus. tools/g25_fixtures.py still reports typedProjectionFields 55 and tools/g25-oracle.mts 46 roots / 15658 outcomes (attempt-02 checks.json:447, 585), both built from the data-plane augmentation only, and tools/make-red-team-fixtures.mjs (1636 cases) covers the data-plane vendor source.
